items.content_html:
Summary

Update http.headers.Clear-Site-Data.cookies for Safari to mark it as partial_implementation: true with a note that only cookies matching the response host are cleared.

Test results and supporting details

  • Safari removes only cookies whose domain exactly matches the response host; cookies set with a Domain attribute are kept, which diverges from the Clear-Site-Data specification requiring registrable domain cookie clearing.
  • Documented and tracked in WebKit bug 325085 (https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=325085).
  • Root cause identified in WebKit source (NetworkStorageSession::deleteCookies in Source/WebKit/NetworkProcess/cocoa/NetworkStorageSessionCocoa.mm), where host-exact matching (domain == String(cookie.domain)) is used.
  • Tested and reproduced on macOS Safari and iOS/iPadOS Safari.
  • All local linter and unit tests (npm run fix, npm test) passed.

Related issues

Fixes #30649
items.title: Clear-Site-Data: Mark cookies directive as partial in Safari

items.content_html:
Description

Fixes #29241

Following the guidance in the issue, this adds a vertical_oriented_table_cells sub-feature to css.properties.writing-mode, mirroring the existing vertical_oriented_form_controls sub-feature.

Data and sources:

  • Chrome 92: verified by testing in the issue; tracking bug referenced via impl_url (crbug.com/40183612).
  • Firefox 47: supports vertical table cells, but rendering is not always correct (see screenshot in the issue), so it is marked as partial_implementation.
  • Safari 17.4: marked as partial_implementation. The change enabling vertical writing modes for table cells (WebKit commit 0d69581) shipped in the WebKit 618.1.10 branch (Safari 17.4), but the follow-up fix was reverted in bug 266941 and the tracking bug 266928 is still open, so support remains incomplete. The note on the entry explains that vertical writing modes were not applied to th and td elements before Safari 17.4, as requested in the issue.
  • All other browsers use mirror.

Questions for reviewers:

  1. Should Firefox's partial_implementation flag start at 47, or is there a later version where rendering is correct?
  2. The issue title says "iOS < 17", but based on the WebKit commit history, 17.4 seems to be the first version with any (partial) support — Safari iOS therefore mirrors 17.4.

Release note

  • CSS: Added vertical_oriented_table_cells subfeature to writing-mode.
items.title: Add vertically-oriented table cells sub-feature to writing-mode

items.content_html:
Summary

Adds the missing compatibility data for the following menus.update() properties:

  • icons — Firefox 64
  • viewTypes — Firefox 64
  • visible — Firefox 63

Additional details

The compatibility data was added after investigating the Firefox WebExtensions implementation and documentation, Firefox release notes, and the related Mozilla Bugzilla issues.

The Firefox version information is based on the following sources:

  • menus.update.visible — Firefox 63, based on Firefox 63 release information and Bug 1482529.
  • menus.update.icons — Firefox 64, based on Firefox 64 release information and Bug 1414566.
  • menus.update.viewTypes — Firefox 64, based on Firefox 64 release information and Bug 1416839.

These properties were already part of the menus.update() API surface, but were not represented as individual compatibility subfeatures in BCD.

The three properties have therefore been added as separate subfeatures under webextensions.api.menus.update, following the existing BCD structure for WebExtensions API parameters and properties.

For browser support values outside Firefox, the entries follow the existing BCD compatibility data and mirroring conventions. In particular, safari_ios is represented as mirror for icons and viewTypes where the BCD linter confirms that the value can be automatically mirrored from Safari.

Related issues

Fixes #30615
items.title: fix(webextensions): add menus.update property compatibility data
